summary: Checks whether a value is **not** a symbol.
description: `nonSymbol(value)` is the same test as `!isSymbol(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.
Registered symbols from `Symbol.for` and the well-known symbols both pass; nothing else does.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is not a symbol; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
nonSymbol("id"); // => true
nonSymbol(null); // => true
nonSymbol(Symbol("id")); // => false
nonSymbol(Symbol.iterator); // => false
```
